letter.bill_summary: Klinik Kasih Private Hospital sent me a bill for RM5,347.70 on 22 Jul 2026. I found some suspicious charges that need to be verified: duplicate billing for GP consultations and Full Blood Count tests, and very high prices for certain medications.
letter.your_rights:
- You have the right to an itemised bill under the Private Hospitals and Medical Procedures Act 1998 (PHFSA 1998).
- You have the right to request clarification on any charge if you are unsure about its validity or reasonableness.
- You can file a complaint with the Ministry of Health Malaysia within 10 working days of receiving your bill if you are not satisfied with the response from the hospital.
- You can also contact the Malaysian Medical Council for doctor-related issues and the Tribunal Tuntutan Pengguna Malaysia for billing disputes under RM50,000.
action_steps: Call the Hospital Patient Relations Officer at Klinik Kasih Private Hospital to discuss your concerns about the bill.
Request an itemised bill from the hospital to verify the charges.
Contact the MOH Pharmaceutical Services Programme to report the high prices of certain medications and request a review.
If you are not satisfied with the response from the hospital, file a complaint with the Ministry of Health Malaysia within 10 working days.
Consider contacting the Malaysian Medical Council for doctor-related issues if necessary.
letter.escalation_guide: If the hospital does not respond within 10 working days or refuses to address your concerns, you can escalate the matter to: Hospital CEO/Management; Ministry of Health Malaysia complaint portal at myhealth.gov.my or call 1-800-88-1000; Malaysian Medical Council (MMC) for doctor-related issues at mmc.gov.my; Tribunal Tuntutan Pengguna Malaysia (Consumer Claims Tribunal) for billing disputes under RM50,000 at ttpm.kpdnhep.gov.my.

KLINIK KASIH PRIVATE HOSPITAL

Re: Formal Inquiry Regarding Invoice Dated 22 JUL 2026 -- Patient: AHMAD HARUN BIN ABDUL KHALID

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to request clarification on several charges in my recent bill (total RM5,347.70), which appear to exceed the legal maximum fee set by PHFSA Schedule 13, or which Parliament's Public Accounts Committee (PAC Report, June 2026) found should not be billed as separate line items.

Items worth querying:
  - GP Consultation - Initial Visit: billed RM100.0 (reference RM125) -- This item appears more than once on your bill. Please verify both charges were for separate, distinct services. [Line-item duplicate detection]
  - GP Consultation - Follow-up: billed RM70.0 (reference RM125) -- This item appears more than once on your bill. Please verify both charges were for separate, distinct services. [Line-item duplicate detection]
  - Full Blood Count (FBC): billed RM60.0 (reference RM80) -- This item appears more than once on your bill. Please verify both charges were for separate, distinct services. [Line-item duplicate detection]
  - Full Blood Count (FBC): billed RM60.0 (reference RM80) -- This item appears more than once on your bill. Please verify both charges were for separate, distinct services. [Line-item duplicate detection]
  - Paracetamol 500mg tablet: billed RM3000.0 (reference RM0.7) -- This drug is priced at RM30.00/unit. The MOH Medicine Price Guide (MyPriMe) lists the reference price at RM0.70/unit. This is 42.9x the reference price. [MyPriMe, MOH Pharmaceutical Services Programme]
  - Metformin 500mg tablet: billed RM100.0 (reference RM0.5) -- This drug is priced at RM2.00/unit. The MOH Medicine Price Guide (MyPriMe) lists the reference price at RM0.50/unit. This is 4.0x the reference price. [MyPriMe, MOH Pharmaceutical Services Programme]
  - Vital Signs Monitoring (daily): billed RM50.0 (reference N/A) -- This charge has been identified by health experts and parliamentary testimony as a potential unbundling concern — worth querying with your hospital. [PAC 1,999-Page Report — AIA CEO Heng Zee Wang, June 19, 2025]

I would appreciate a written explanation for each item above, and a corrected invoice where applicable. This letter is a request for clarification, not an accusation of wrongdoing.

I look forward to your response within 10 working days as provided under the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998.

Yours faithfully,
AHMAD HARUN BIN ABDUL KHALID
